generation_prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: production RGBA texture atlas for whole-tree impostor cards in a realistic European hill-town game.
Primary request: a square atlas containing EXACTLY SIXTEEN different mature broadleaf trees, in a perfectly regular FOUR BY FOUR grid of equal square cells. Background must be genuinely transparent, including the gaps between leaves and branches. There are no grid lines or labels.

Composition: each cell contains one complete, separate tree, upright and seen from a horizontal side view with a little natural perspective. Every tree fits wholly within its own square cell, with clear transparent margin on every side. Each tree's highest leaf is about 8% below its cell top and its trunk base about 8% above the cell bottom. Crowns may be broad but must never touch neighboring cells. Keep all sixteen similarly framed. Prefer a detailed 2048-by-2048 square output.

Rows, left to right:
Row 1: four visibly distinct deciduous European oaks: an asymmetric spreading forked crown, an irregular tall lobed crown, a broad low crown with a broken top, and a wind-shaped leaning crown.
Row 2: four different holm oaks: dense low rounded but strongly asymmetric, a taller narrow multi-lobed one, a wide layered multi-stem one, and an irregular leaning one.
Row 3: four different European beeches: tall oval, broad and layered, narrow with a broken outline, and an old spreading specimen with an off-centre top.
Row 4: four different mature willows: irregular tall drooping, broad low drooping, narrow leaning, and layered asymmetrical drooping.

Style: convincing photographic whole trees with real branch structure, uneven interlocking foliage masses, small irregular gaps and varied silhouettes. Dense foliage continues fairly low so this can form continuous hillside woodland. Muted summer forest greens and restrained olive greens, visibly darker recesses inside each crown, subtle species variation. Fine leaves should support the large crown masses rather than form high-contrast speckles.
Lighting: soft neutral overcast daylight, no hard directional sun or cast shadows, no rim light, no glossy white leaf highlights. The game supplies sunlight and fog.
Constraints: preserve real alpha. No opaque backdrop, black or white halo, checkerboard pixels, sky, landscape, ground plane, roots spreading across a floor, shadows on the background, people, conifers, ornaments, text, border or watermark. Do not repeat the same tree shape, mirror copies, stamp circular lollipop crowns, or make a flat illustration. This is an isolated tree texture atlas, not a scene or contact sheet of forest photographs.
spacing_edit_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the supplied sixteen-tree RGBA atlas.
Keep the same sixteen tree species, four-by-four row order, photographic foliage, muted summer colours and soft diffuse lighting. Fix ONLY atlas separation and cutout cleanliness.

Recompose every individual tree entirely inside its own equal square cell in the exact regular four-by-four grid. Shrink each whole tree around its own centre until its bounding box occupies at most 72% of that cell's width and 78% of its height. Each cell must have at least 12% clear transparent padding left and right and at least 10% padding above and below. This applies to ALL branches and leaves. No two trees may touch, overlap, cross a cell boundary, or be cropped at the outside of the image. Keep trees individually centred and upright, without stretching them. In particular separate the broad second-row crowns and the wide last-row willows.
Remove little ground/shadow patches beneath the trunks. Clean the cutout edges: retain fine real leaves and natural semi-transparent leaf edges, but remove yellow/green matte fringes and detached background specks.
The gutters, outer border, gaps between leaves and all background must be genuine alpha transparency, never solid black, green, white or checkerboard pixels. No labels, grid lines, text or new objects.
The result is a practical whole-tree texture atlas for game cards. Preserve the sixteen different silhouettes and their interior photographic detail; do not redesign or replace the trees. Keep a square image.
state: source atlas prepared; not installed or natively reviewed
uv_method: Read-only alpha component analysis finds sixteen separate trees. Numeric per-tree UV rectangles follow the actual layout rather than clipping to the requested regular grid; no pixels, masks or alpha were changed.
